text:
mira: Quick sync — merged the runtime/dashboard PR that adds per-model token_throughput, kv_cache_hit_rate, and slo_burn_5m (new derived metric) for the last 72h. Before we enable alerts I want cross-team agreement on thresholds, SLO burn semantics, and exact pager routing.

dan: Thanks — can you list the metric names as exported? We need stable label keys for routing (team, model, deployment). Also confirm slo_burn_5m is a rate (0..1) or a count.

mira: metric names: 
- runtime_token_throughput_total (counter)
- kv_cache_hits_total / kv_cache_requests_total (counters; we expose kv_cache_hit_rate as gauge)
- slo_burn_5m (gauge, ratio 0..5, where 1 == exact burn rate of 1)
labels: team, model, region, deployment_id.

samira: Telemetry notes: ingestion pipeline normalizes labels to low-cardinality for model (we keep model_family not full model hash) and map deployment_id -> deployment_owner. We'll add a telemetry tag `service=runtime` for easier dashboard filtering. High cardinality tag candidates: user_id, request_id are dropped before storage.

jess: From SRE perspective: propose two tiered alerts based on slo_burn_5m:
1) page (P1) if slo_burn_5m > 1.0 for 10m AND token_throughput > 1000 (indicates sustained traffic causing burn).
2) page (P2) if slo_burn_5m > 0.5 for 30m.
3) notify (email/ops Slack) if slo_burn_5m > 0.2 for 60m.
Rationale: avoid noisy pages on short spikes. Also want an early-warning metric: increasing kv_cache_miss_rate precedes burn — suggest adding kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.1 for 15m as a warning.

jess: Example PromQL for P1 (draft):
```
expr = (avg_over_time(slo_burn_5m[10m]) > 1.0) and (avg_over_time(runtime_token_throughput_total[10m]) > 1000)
for = 10m
labels: severity=page, pager_team=runtime-oncall
annotations: runbook="https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-slo-burn", dashboard="{{ dashboard_link }}"
```

leo: UX/Console note — need a per-deployment toggle in dashboard to opt out/in alerts (customer-admins for dedicated/private). Also expose a rollout flag so PMs can enable alerts in canary. Alerts should default to notify only for newly onboarded models for first 48h.

pm: (typo correction) — oops ignore

pk: Infra constraints: evaluation of slo_burn_5m across all models at 1m resolution is expensive. Can we limit alerting queries to label `deployment_id=active` or add precomputed aggregates per-team? If not, we need quota for increased query QPS. Also quantify storage cost if we keep 72h at 1m resolution.

dan: For routing: prefer label-based routing to map to the right PD escalation policy. We should add `pager_team` label at alert time (runtime-oncall, infra-oncall, se-team). If model has enterprise_owner label we should route initial notifications to that owner (notify channel) and keep paging to runtime-oncall only when severity=page.

mira: Agreed. We'll ensure alert rules set `pager_team` and `deployment_owner`. For enterprise customers we set `notify_channel=customers/<org>` so PMs can triage before paging.

jess: Escalation policy idea: P1 -> page runtime-oncall immediate -> 5m -> page infra-oncall -> 10m -> page eng-sre lead. P2 -> page runtime-oncall after 10m. Need PD policies created; @oncall-bot can you create placeholders? :slightly_smiling_face:

oncall-bot: Created PagerDuty escalation stub: PD-policy-id=PD-97531, routes: [runtime-oncall, infra-oncall, eng-sre-lead]. Link: https://pagerduty.internal/policies/PD-97531

samira: I'll add telemetry alerts for ingestion lag (if telemetry pipeline is delayed >5m we should suppress slo alerts or annotate them). We'll add `telemetry_ok` label to alerts that are only valid when pipeline is healthy.

mira: Can we agree on final numeric thresholds? Proposal: P1 threshold = slo_burn_5m > 1.0 for 10m with throughput floor 1000. P2 threshold = slo_burn_5m > 0.6 for 20m. Notify threshold = slo_burn_5m > 0.25 for 60m. Kv cache warning = kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.12 for 15m. Thoughts?

jess: +1 to numbers, prefer 0.6 for P2 instead of 0.5 to reduce noise. Add `for` durations to reduce flapping.

dan: One gotcha: some legacy deployments report throughput under a different metric name; I'll add a mapping layer in the alerting templating so older deployments are included.

leo: UX/rollout: I'll add a console toggle and a per-deployment audit log entry when alerts are changed. Also wire a small banner showing which alerts are active for the selected model.

pk: Let's schedule a small load test before enabling pages. If burn fires during chaos or synthetic traffic we should ensure PD policies are tested.

mira: Action items:
- samira: add telemetry_ok flag and make telemetry annotations (by EOD).
- dan: add legacy-metric mappings for throughput (tomorrow).
- jess: create the PD policies & alert rule PR with PromQL and runbook links (today).
- leo: add console toggle & audit log (next week).
- pk: schedule synthetic exercise to validate pages (next week).

mira: I'll hold the alert flip in the dashboard until PD policies are in place and we've run the synthetic. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

samira: will send numbers on ingestion cost after I run the aggregate query sizing.

jess: ping me when PD policy is created, I'll review runbooks.

dan: tagging internal owners on the PR once ready.

mira: closing the thread — we'll reconvene if any blocker pops up. Thanks! :rocket:
